slides.title: Multiple Linear Regression I
slides.subtitle: Methods, interpretation, fit, inference, and special variables
slides.speaker_notes: This chapter extends simple linear regression to settings with several explanatory variables. The framework retains familiar ideas such as goodness of fit and t-based inference while allowing flexible functions of explanatory variables.
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_014 - 3 Multiple Linear Regression - I.tex

slides.title: Motivating Example: Term Life Insurance
slides.subtitle: Demand for policy face amount
slides.speaker_notes: The analysis focuses on households that purchased term life insurance and asks which characteristics influence the amount purchased. Logarithmic transformations of face amount and income help represent a relationship that is more nearly linear.
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_014 - 3 Multiple Linear Regression - I.tex

slides.title: Exploring Multivariate Data
slides.subtitle: Before fitting a model
slides.speaker_notes: Scatterplot matrices and correlation tables are useful first summaries of multivariate data. However, correlation measures linear pairwise association and can miss nonlinear patterns or relationships that emerge only after controlling for other variables.
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_014 - 3 Multiple Linear Regression - I.tex

slides.title: Least Squares Regression Plane
slides.subtitle: Fitting several explanatory variables
slides.speaker_notes: Because a single plane usually cannot pass through all observations, least squares selects coefficients that minimize the sum of squared vertical deviations. For term life insurance, the fitted model is \(\widehat{y}=2.584+0.206x_{1}+0.306x_{2}+0.494x_{3}\).
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_014 - 3 Multiple Linear Regression - I.tex

slides.title: Matrix Formulation
slides.subtitle: Normal equations and coefficient estimator
slides.speaker_notes: Matrix notation makes the least-squares solution compact and scalable. A unique formula requires that the explanatory variables not be linear combinations of one another, so that \(\mathbf{X}'\mathbf{X}\) is invertible.
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_014 - 3 Multiple Linear Regression - I.tex

slides.title: Regression Function and Assumptions
slides.subtitle: Interpretation and sampling framework
slides.speaker_notes: For a continuous explanatory variable, \(\beta_j\) is the expected change in the response per unit change in \(x_j\), holding the other explanatory variables fixed. The model may be nonlinear in explanatory variables while remaining linear in its parameters.
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_014 - 3 Multiple Linear Regression - I.tex

slides.title: Properties of Least Squares Estimators
slides.subtitle: Precision and distribution
slides.speaker_notes: Under assumptions F1 through F4, least squares coefficients are unbiased and have the stated covariance matrix. With normal responses or errors, the coefficient vector is normally distributed, supporting later statistical inference.
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_014 - 3 Multiple Linear Regression - I.tex

slides.title: Goodness of Fit
slides.subtitle: Residual variation and explained variation
bullets: Total SS = Error SS + Regression SS
slides.speaker_notes: The residual standard deviation is the typical error about the fitted regression plane. While \(R^2\) is the proportion of response variability explained by the regression, it never decreases when a variable is added; adjusted \(R^2\) accounts for degrees of freedom.
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_014 - 3 Multiple Linear Regression - I.tex

slides.title: Inference and Added Variable Plots
slides.subtitle: Assessing one explanatory variable
slides.speaker_notes: The t-ratio measures how many estimated standard errors a coefficient is from zero; as a rule of thumb, an absolute t-ratio exceeding two indicates an important variable. Added variable plots compare residualized response and residualized predictor values, revealing the relationship after controlling for the remaining predictors.
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_014 - 3 Multiple Linear Regression - I.tex

slides.title: Special Explanatory Variables
slides.subtitle: Flexible models within linear regression
slides.speaker_notes: Binary variables represent group differences relative to a base category. Transformations and interactions permit nonlinear response patterns and slopes that depend on other explanatory variables, while the model remains linear in the coefficients.
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_014 - 3 Multiple Linear Regression - I.tex

slides.title: What to Carry Away
slides.subtitle: Multiple linear regression foundations
slides.speaker_notes: Multiple linear regression summarizes complex multivariate data using a model that is linear in parameters. Effective analysis combines exploratory graphics, meaningful coefficient interpretation, diagnostics of fit, inference, and thoughtful choices of variables and transformations.
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_014 - 3 Multiple Linear Regression - I.tex
